proofs.proof_tex:
For either prior, introduce unit-level arm values \(X_{i1}\) and \(X_{i0}\) by
\[
(X_{i1},X_{i0})=
\begin{cases}
(U_i,U_i),&\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{same}},\\
(U_i,V_i),&\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{ind}},
\end{cases}
\qquad d_i=X_{i1}-X_{i0},
\]
where the displayed signs are independent Rademacher variables except for the equality imposed under \(\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{same}}\).  These priors give the additive schedules
\[
h_{z,n}(A)=\frac1M\sum_{i\in A}X_{iz},
\qquad
\tau_n=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n d_i.                                      \tag{1}
\]
All expectations in the calculation below are joint over the indicated prior and the two-stage design unless conditioning is displayed.  Write \(G=G_n\), \(N=N_n\), and \(q_n=1-p_n\).  Assumption~\ref{ass:stable-treatment-fraction} supplies a constant \(\delta>0\) such that \(p_n,q_n\geq\delta\) for all sufficiently large \(n\).

We first split the Doob martingale at the end of the unit-permutation reveal.  Given the realized blocks, complete randomization of the labels gives
\[
\mathbb E[\widehat\tau_n\mid\mathbf A_n]
=\frac1G\sum_{g=1}^G\{h_{1,n}(A_{ng})-h_{0,n}(A_{ng})\}
=\frac1N\sum_{r=1}^N d_{U_r}.
\]
For
\[
c_g=\frac{h_{1,n}(A_{ng})}{p_n}
    +\frac{h_{0,n}(A_{ng})}{q_n},
\]
direct subtraction of this conditional mean from the estimator in Definition~\ref{def:pame-estimator} gives
\[
\widehat\tau_n-\mathbb E[\widehat\tau_n\mid\mathbf A_n]
=\frac1G\sum_{g=1}^G(Z_{ng}-p_n)c_g.                                  \tag{2}
\]
Because the unit permutation is revealed completely before any label and the label permutation is independent of it by Definition~\ref{def:random-partition-design}, equations (1)--(2) decompose the predictable variation as
\[
Q_n=Q_n^U+Q_n^L,                                                       \tag{3}
\]
where the superscripts denote the unit- and label-reveal phases.

Let \(L_n=n-N\).  Just before unit reveal \(r\), let \(\mu_{r-1}^d\) and
\[
v_{r-1}^d=\frac1{n-r+1}\sum_{i\ {\rm remaining}}
                 (d_i-\mu_{r-1}^d)^2
\]
be the mean and denominator-population variance of the remaining values.  When \(N<n\), subtracting the conditional expected sample mean before and after reveal \(r\) yields
\[
D_{n,r}^U=\frac{L_n}{N(n-r)}(d_{U_r}-\mu_{r-1}^d),
\qquad
Q_n^U=\sum_{r=1}^{N}\frac{L_n^2}{N^2(n-r)^2}v_{r-1}^d.                 \tag{4}
\]
When \(N=n\), the selected-sample mean equals the population mean identically, so \(Q_n^U=0\).

Under \(\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{same}}\), every \(d_i=0\), hence \(Q_n^U=0\).  Under \(\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{ind}}\), the randomly permuted \(d_i\)'s are independent, have mean zero, variance two, and satisfy \(|d_i|\leq2\).  For a remaining population of size \(m\), expansion of its empirical first and second moments and Cauchy--Schwarz give
\[
\mathbb E|v_{r-1}^d-2|\leq C m^{-1/2},
\qquad m=n-r+1,                                                       \tag{5}
\]
for a universal finite constant \(C\).  Define the deterministic coefficient sum
\[
S_n
=G\sum_{r=1}^{N}\frac{L_n^2}{N^2(n-r)^2}
=\frac{L_n^2}{MN}\sum_{j=L_n}^{n-1}j^{-2},                            \tag{6}
\]
when \(L_n\geq1\), and put \(S_n=0\) when \(L_n=0\).  If \(0<\rho<1\), the integral comparison for the decreasing function \(x^{-2}\), together with \(N/n\to\rho\), gives
\[
S_n\longrightarrow\frac{1-\rho}{M}.                                  \tag{7}
\]
Moreover, every remaining population in (4) has size at least \(L_n+1\asymp n\); hence (5) and (6) imply
\[
\mathbb E|GQ_n^U-2S_n|
\leq C(L_n+1)^{-1/2}S_n\longrightarrow0.                              \tag{8}
\]
If \(\rho=1\) and \(L_n\geq1\), another integral comparison gives
\[
0\leq S_n
\leq\frac{L_n^2}{MN}\left(\frac1{L_n^2}+\frac1{L_n}\right)
=\frac{1+L_n}{MN}\longrightarrow0,                                   \tag{9}
\]
because \(L_n/n\to0\) and \(N/n\to1\).  The bound \(v_{r-1}^d\leq4\) then makes \(GQ_n^U\leq4S_n\to0\).  Equations (7)--(9) prove
\[
GQ_n^U\xrightarrow{L^1}
\begin{cases}
0,&\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{same}},\\
2(1-\rho)/M,&\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{ind}}.
\end{cases}                                                           \tag{10}
\]

We next reveal the labels.  Just before label \(s\), let
\[
\pi_{s-1}=\frac{G_{1n}-\sum_{j<s}Z_{nj}}{G-s+1},
\qquad
\bar c_{s+1:G}=\frac1{G-s}\sum_{j>s}c_j.
\]
Taking successive conditional expectations in (2) gives, for \(s<G\),
\[
D_{n,N+s}^L
=\frac{Z_{ns}-\pi_{s-1}}G(c_s-\bar c_{s+1:G}),                       \tag{11}
\]
while the final label is determined and has zero increment.  Therefore
\[
GQ_n^L
=\frac1G\sum_{s=1}^{G-1}\pi_{s-1}(1-\pi_{s-1})
                  (c_s-\bar c_{s+1:G})^2.                             \tag{12}
\]
The label process is independent of \((c_1,\ldots,c_G)\).  If \(K=G-s+1\) labels remain, elementary sampling-without-replacement covariance algebra gives
\[
\mathbb E(\pi_{s-1}-p_n)^2
=p_nq_n\frac{G-K}{K(G-1)}.                                            \tag{13}
\]
Since \(|x(1-x)-p_nq_n|\leq2|x-p_n|\), since \(|c_g|\leq p_n^{-1}+q_n^{-1}\leq2/\delta\), and since \(G^{-1}\sum_{K=2}^G K^{-1/2}=O(G^{-1/2})\), equations (12)--(13) and Cauchy--Schwarz imply
\[
GQ_n^L-\frac{p_nq_n}{G}\sum_{s=1}^{G-1}
                    (c_s-\bar c_{s+1:G})^2\xrightarrow{L^1}0.         \tag{14}
\]

Under either prior, the disjoint blocks use disjoint collections of independent signs.  Consequently, jointly over the unit permutation and the prior, \(c_1,\ldots,c_G\) are independent and identically distributed, centered, and uniformly bounded.  The reverse updating identity
\[
\sum_{s=1}^{G-1}\frac{G-s}{G-s+1}(c_s-\bar c_{s+1:G})^2
=\sum_{g=1}^{G}(c_g-\bar c)^2                                        \tag{15}
\]
follows by expanding the two sides recursively.  The absolute difference between the unweighted sum in (14) and the left side of (15) is at most
\[
4(2/\delta)^2\sum_{K=2}^G K^{-1}=O(\log G).                           \tag{16}
\]
The bounded triangular-array law of large numbers applied to the right side of (15), together with (16) and Assumption~\ref{ass:group-count-growth}, now gives
\[
\frac1G\sum_{s=1}^{G-1}(c_s-\bar c_{s+1:G})^2
-\operatorname{Var}(c_1)\xrightarrow{L^2}0.                           \tag{17}
\]
Direct calculation from (1) gives
\[
\operatorname{Var}(c_1)=
\begin{cases}
[Mp_n^2q_n^2]^{-1},&\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{same}},\\
M^{-1}(p_n^{-2}+q_n^{-2}),&\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{ind}}.
\end{cases}                                                           \tag{18}
\]
Equations (12)--(18) and \(p_n\to p\), \(q_n\to q=1-p\), prove
\[
GQ_n^L\xrightarrow{L^1}
\begin{cases}
[Mpq]^{-1},&\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{same}},\\
M^{-1}(q/p+p/q),&\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{ind}}.
\end{cases}                                                           \tag{19}
\]

The coefficient sum \(S_n\) is at most \(1/M\), because (6) contains \(N\) summands, each at most \(L_n^{-2}\).  Thus (4) implies \(GQ_n^U\leq4/M\).  Equation (12) and the uniform bound on \(c_g\) likewise give a deterministic constant bounding \(GQ_n^L\).  Hence the \(L^1\) convergences in (10) and (19) upgrade to \(L^2\) convergence.  Adding them and using
\[
\frac qp+\frac pq+2=\frac1{pq}
\]
establishes
\[
G_nQ_n\xrightarrow{L^2}
\begin{cases}
[Mp(1-p)]^{-1},&\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{same}},\\
[Mp(1-p)]^{-1}-2\rho/M,&\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{ind}}.
\end{cases}                                                           \tag{20}
\]
In particular, \(\operatorname{Var}(G_nQ_n)\to0\), which is the required normalized predictable-variation check.

Because the proposed scope has \(\rho>0\), Proposition~\ref{prop:rademacher-mixture-separation} applies and gives convergence in prior probability of \(G_n\sigma_n^2\) to the same respective constants.  Both constants are positive: the independent-prior constant is at least \(2/M\), since \(p(1-p)\leq1/4\) and \(\rho\leq1\).  Equation (20) and division by a random denominator bounded away from zero in probability therefore give
\[
Q_n/\sigma_n^2\xrightarrow{p}1                                      \tag{21}
\]
jointly over prior and design.  For fixed \(\varepsilon>0\), put
\[
b_n(Y)=\mathbb P_{\mathbf A_n,\mathbf Z_n}
\left(\left.|Q_n/\sigma_n^2-1|>\varepsilon\,\right|Y\right).
\]
By iterated expectation, (21) says \(\mathbb E_{\mathbb H_n}b_n(Y)\to0\).  Markov's inequality then yields
\[
\mathbb P_{\mathbb H_n}\{b_n(Y)>\varepsilon\}
\leq\varepsilon^{-1}\mathbb E_{\mathbb H_n}b_n(Y)\longrightarrow0,
\]
which is the final assertion.

Let \(j\in\{\mathrm{same},\mathrm{ind}\}\), and write \(d_j\) for the corresponding constant in the theorem.  Proposition~\ref{prop:rademacher-mixture-separation} gives
\[
G_n\sigma_n^2\xrightarrow{p}d_j                                     \tag{1}
\]
under \(\mathbb H_n^j\).  For \(t>0\), define the schedule-measurable conditional tail probability
\[
b_{n,t}(Y)=
\mathbb P_{\mathbf A_n,\mathbf Z_n}
\left(\left.|Q_n/\sigma_n^2-1|>t\,\right|Y\right).
\]
Lemma~\ref{lem:rademacher-predictable-variation}, whose positive-density scope agrees with \(\rho\in(0,1]\), gives for each fixed integer \(k\geq1\)
\[
\mathbb H_n^j\{b_{n,1/k}(Y)>1/k\}\longrightarrow0.                   \tag{2}
\]
Set
\[
E_{n,k}^j=
\left\{Y:\ |G_n\sigma_n^2(Y)-d_j|\leq k^{-1},\quad
                 b_{n,1/k}(Y)\leq k^{-1}\right\}.                    \tag{3}
\]
Equations (1)--(2) imply \(\mathbb H_n^j(E_{n,k}^j)\to1\) for every fixed \(k\).

We record the elementary diagonal selection explicitly.  Choose increasing integers \(m_k\) such that, for both values of \(j\),
\[
n\geq m_k\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\mathbb H_n^j(E_{n,k}^j)\geq1-k^{-1}.
\]
After increasing them if necessary, take \(m_{k+1}>m_k\).  For \(n\geq m_1\), define \(k_n=\max\{k:m_k\leq n\}\), while for \(n<m_1\) put \(k_n=1\).  Then \(k_n\to\infty\).  With
\[
\Gamma_n^j=
\begin{cases}
E_{n,k_n}^j,&n\geq m_1,\\
\operatorname{supp}(\mathbb H_n^j),&n<m_1,
\end{cases}                                                           \tag{4}
\]
we have \(\mathbb H_n^j(\Gamma_n^j)\to1\), and, for \(n\geq m_1\), uniformly on \(\Gamma_n^j\),
\[
|G_n\sigma_n^2(Y)-d_j|\leq k_n^{-1}.                                  \tag{5}
\]

Every schedule row in \(\Gamma_n^j\) is additive and satisfies \(|Y_{i,n}(z,A)|=1\leq B\).  The deterministic design sequences satisfy Assumptions~\ref{ass:group-count-growth}, \ref{ass:stable-treatment-fraction}, and \ref{ass:sampling-fraction}.  Since \(d_j>c_\sigma\), equation (5) implies the scaled-variance lower bound along every Cartesian selection \((Y_n)_{n\geq1}\in\prod_n\Gamma_n^j\).  Under the repaired Definition~\ref{def:dense-schedule-class}, these are exactly the remaining membership requirements, so every such selection belongs to \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{dense}}\).

The construction has a stronger property that is not required for membership in the repaired ambient class.  For fixed \(\varepsilon>0\), eventually \(k_n^{-1}<\varepsilon\), and (3)--(4) imply, for every \(Y_n\in\Gamma_n^j\),
\[
\mathbb P_{\mathbf A_n,\mathbf Z_n}
\left(\left.|Q_n/\sigma_n^2-1|>\varepsilon\,\right|Y_n\right)
\leq b_{n,1/k_n}(Y_n)
\leq k_n^{-1}\longrightarrow0.                                       \tag{6}
\]
Thus the additive lower-bound supports satisfy predictable quadratic-variation stability by the construction-specific Lemma~\ref{lem:rademacher-predictable-variation}, even though \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{dense}}\) no longer assumes it.  This is the promised subclass certificate.

Let \(\widetilde{\mathbb H}_n^j\) be \(\mathbb H_n^j\) conditioned on \(\Gamma_n^j\), and let \(P_n^j\) be its image under the design-and-observation Markov kernel into \(\mathcal O_n\).  Conditioning changes a prior by total variation at most \(\mathbb H_n^j((\Gamma_n^j)^c)=o(1)\), and a Markov kernel contracts total variation.  Proposition~\ref{prop:rademacher-mixture-separation} says that the two unconditioned observation mixtures are exactly equal.  The triangle inequality therefore yields
\[
\|P_n^{\mathrm{same}}-P_n^{\mathrm{ind}}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}=o(1).         \tag{7}
\]

Put \(a=d_{\mathrm{same}}\), \(b=d_{\mathrm{ind}}\), and
\[
\Delta=a-b=2\rho/M>0.
\]
Choose \(0<\varepsilon<\Delta/(4a)\).  From (5), for all sufficiently large \(n\), the event
\[
\left|\widehat S_n/\sigma_n^2-1\right|\leq\varepsilon                 \tag{8}
\]
implies
\[
G_n\widehat S_n>(a+b)/2
\quad\text{on }\Gamma_n^{\mathrm{same}},
\qquad
G_n\widehat S_n<(a+b)/2
\quad\text{on }\Gamma_n^{\mathrm{ind}}.                               \tag{9}
\]
Indeed, as the uniform error in (5) tends to zero,
\[
(1-\varepsilon)(a-o(1))-(a+b)/2
\geq\Delta/2-\varepsilon a-o(1)>0,
\]
and
\[
(a+b)/2-(1+\varepsilon)(b+o(1))
\geq\Delta/2-\varepsilon a-o(1)>0.
\]

Use the measurable test that declares \(\mathrm{same}\) exactly when \(G_n\widehat S_n>(a+b)/2\).  By (8)--(9), the event that \(\widehat S_n\) has relative error at most \(\varepsilon\) implies correct classification under either conditioned prior.  Therefore the sum of testing-error probabilities is at most the sum of the two mixture probabilities of relative estimation error greater than \(\varepsilon\).

For completeness, if \(T_n\) is the test's \(\mathrm{same}\) decision set, then
\[
P_n^{\mathrm{same}}(T_n^c)+P_n^{\mathrm{ind}}(T_n)
=1-P_n^{\mathrm{same}}(T_n)+P_n^{\mathrm{ind}}(T_n)
\geq1-\|P_n^{\mathrm{same}}-P_n^{\mathrm{ind}}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}.
\]
Combining this inequality with (7) shows that the larger of the two mixture risks satisfies
\[
\max_{j\in\{\mathrm{same},\mathrm{ind}\}}
\int
\mathbb P_{\mathbf A_n,\mathbf Z_n}
\left(\left.
\left|\widehat S_n/\sigma_n^2-1\right|>\varepsilon
\right|Y\right)
\,d\widetilde{\mathbb H}_n^j(Y)
\geq\frac12-o(1).                                                     \tag{10}
\]

Each row in \(\Gamma_n^j\) can be extended to an infinite array in \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{dense}}\): keep that row at index \(n\) and choose any member of \(\Gamma_m^j\) at every sufficiently large \(m\neq n\), with arbitrary bounded rows at the finitely many earlier indices.  The sets are nonempty eventually because their prior probabilities tend to one, and the resulting Cartesian selection obeys the deterministic fraction limits, the envelope, and, by (5), \(\liminf_mG_m\sigma_m^2=d_j>c_\sigma\).  Thus each average risk in (10) is bounded above by
\[
\sup_{Y\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{dense}}}
\Pr_Y\left(\left|\frac{\widehat S_n}{\sigma_n^2}-1\right|
>\varepsilon\right).
\]
Taking the lower limit proves the asserted lower bound \(1/2\).  The support schedules are additive and have no composition interference, and hence form a subclass of the arbitrary bounded composition-interference schedules.  The impossibility on this subclass therefore transfers upward to the entire repaired ambient class.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: Suppose \(G_n\to\infty\), \(p_n\to p\in(0,1)\), and \(N_n/n\to\rho\in(0,1]\). Under either \(\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{same}}\) or \(\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{ind}}\), the unit-permutation-then-label-permutation predictable variation satisfies, jointly over the prior and design, \[ G_nQ_n\xrightarrow{L^2} \begin{cases} [Mp(1-p)]^{-1},&\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{same}},\\ [Mp(1-p)]^{-1}-2\rho/M,&\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{ind}}. \end{cases} \] Consequently, for every \(\varepsilon>0\), under either prior, \[ \mathbb P_{\mathbb H_n}\!\left\{ \mathbb P_{\mathbf A_n,\mathbf Z_n}\!\left( \left|Q_n/\sigma_n^2-1\right|>\varepsilon\mid Y\right)>\varepsilon \right\}\longrightarrow0. \]
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The current proof obtains the exact-variance limit used in the final ratio statement from Proposition~\ref{prop:rademacher-mixture-separation}, whose separated-limit claim has the positive-density scope \(\rho\in(0,1]\). The impossibility theorem is the substantive consumer and also requires positive density, so restricting this construction-specific lemma to the same regime removes the dependency mismatch without assuming new mathematics.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Predictable quadratic-variation stabilization is not derived from bounded schedules and must not be a membership condition of the ambient dense class. The repaired class retains growth, allocation and sampling limits, bounded support, and scaled-variance nondegeneracy exactly as directed.

proposed.statement: Fix \(M\ge2\), \(p\in(0,1)\), \(\rho\in(0,1]\), \(B\ge1\), and design sequences satisfying the three fraction and growth assumptions. Put \[ d_{\mathrm{same}}=\frac1{Mp(1-p)},\qquad d_{\mathrm{ind}}=\frac1{Mp(1-p)}-\frac{2\rho}{M}, \] and suppose \(0<c_\sigma<d_{\mathrm{ind}}\). There are high-prior-probability sets of deterministic Rademacher schedule rows whose Cartesian diagonal selections all belong to \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{dense}}\); after conditioning \(\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{same}}\) and \(\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{ind}}\) on these sets, their induced one-realization mixture laws have total-variation distance tending to zero, while \(G_n\sigma_n^2\) converges uniformly on the respective supports to \(d_{\mathrm{same}}\) and \(d_{\mathrm{ind}}\). Consequently there exists \(\varepsilon>0\) such that every measurable \(\widehat S_n(\mathcal O_n)\) obeys \[ \liminf_{n\to\infty}\sup_{Y\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{dense}}} \Pr_Y\left(\left|\frac{\widehat S_n}{\sigma_n^2}-1\right|>\varepsilon\right) \ge\frac12. \] Thus no estimator from one realization is uniformly ratio-consistent for the exact variance over the full dense class. The deterministic support arrays, rather than a generally unavailable pair of deterministic arrays with close laws, are the valid diagonal certificate.

proposed_core_edits.reason: After predictable variation is removed from the ambient class, \(Q_n\) is no longer a free symbol of this theorem's own claim; its construction-specific appearance is supplied through the declared Rademacher predictable-variation lemma. The claim and dependency spine are otherwise preserved.

prose_updates.tldr: Randomly formed groups cease to behave as independent regression clusters when a positive fraction of eligible units is partitioned. The normalized Kneser operator gives an unconditional exact variance identity and a schedule-uniform expansion in which only the degree-one Johnson projection of the arm difference survives at first order. The ambient class \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{dense}}\) contains the growth, fraction, boundedness, and scaled-variance conditions, but not predictable quadratic-variation stabilization. The centered Gaussian theorem is instead an implication for each array in that class satisfying the additional filtration-side premise \(Q_n/\sigma_n^2\xrightarrow{p}1\); CR2 studentization and coverage are conditional on the same premise, whereas the variance and CR2 expansions and their ratio comparisons are unconditional. At positive density CR2 is conservative and is ratio-consistent exactly when the projection correction is negligible. At zero density it yields studentized normality without \(N_n^2/n\to0\), conditional on the explicit premise. The eight-unit witness has exact variance \(1/7\) and expected CR2 \(2/7\). No one-realization estimator is uniformly ratio-consistent for exact variance even on the additive no-interference subclass; the Rademacher supports used for that lower bound separately satisfy predictable-variation stability, so the lower bound transfers upward to the enlarged arbitrary-composition class.

project_justification.gap: \cite{FuSamiiWang2026} defines PAME and validates clustered inference by coupling the whole disjoint group tuple to independent draws under its Assumption 1 and \(N_n^2/n\to0\). That approximation discards first-order finite-pool dependence when \(N_n/n\to\rho>0\), while fixed-cluster CR2 does not restore it. Bounded composition schedules also do not by themselves establish predictable quadratic-variation stabilization for the exact reveal filtration.
project_justification.niche: The disjointness relation is a Kneser operator on the uniform \(M\)-slice, so exact causal variance and the CR2 comparison can be decomposed unconditionally by Johnson degree before a Gaussian approximation is invoked. The ambient schedule class is kept separate from the statistic-specific filtration premise, which appears only as an antecedent of the CLT, studentization, and coverage conclusions.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the exact spectrum-weighted variance, the schedule-uniform \(O(n^{-1})\) dense expansion, and the unconditional CR2 fluctuation bound; proves that only degree one survives at the \(G_n\)-scale; and proves centered martingale normality and Wald coverage whenever an array in the ambient class additionally satisfies \(Q_n/\sigma_n^2\xrightarrow{p}1\). It also characterizes the unconditional CR2 sharpness frontier, verifies the versioned \({\tt clubSandwich}\) consumer and the finite witness, and proves an all-statistic exact-variance impossibility theorem using a construction-specific predictable-variation calculation and deterministic diagonal selection.

prose_updates.related_work: \cite{FuSamiiWang2026} is the closest theorem-level comparator: its Section 3 permits a fixed finite menu of group sizes, and its Theorems 1--2 obtain asymptotic normality and CR2 ratio consistency under shared boundedness, their Assumption 1, and \(N_n^2/n\to0\). The present positive theory treats the exact homogeneous \(K=1\) structural subcase. Its exact Kneser variance and CR2 expansions are unconditional under the stated fixed-size design conditions, whereas its Gaussian and coverage conclusions replace the comparator's inference conditions by scaled-variance nondegeneracy and the explicit statistic-specific antecedent \(Q_n/\sigma_n^2\xrightarrow{p}1\). This is an assumption trade, not a pure weakening, because predictable-variation stabilization is not derived for every bounded schedule and is not included in \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{dense}}\). Positive homogeneous conclusions are not claimed for variable group sizes. Theorems 1 and 3 and the Johnson association-scheme discussion of \cite{Filmus2016} provide the harmonic architecture; Proposition 3.1 of \cite{BrouwerEtAl2018} supplies the classical Kneser spectrum, and the present work derives the causal covariance quadratic form. Section 2.2 and Theorems 3--4 of \cite{LiDing2017} inform complete randomization, while \cite{Pollard1984}, Theorem VIII.1, supplies the martingale-array implication once predictable variation and conditional Lindeberg are available. The versioned \({\tt clubSandwich}\) 0.7.0 and \({\tt sandwich}\) 3.1-3 source contracts supply the software assembly, default-target, adjustment, bread, and scale semantics used by the exact consumer proposition; \cite{PustejovskyTipton2018} explains CR2 calibration under independent-cluster working models, and \cite{SuDing2021} gives the fixed-cluster design-based regression comparison. None supplies the random-partition projection correction. \cite{HarshawMiddletonSavje2026} studies optimized estimable conservative quadratic variance bounds when exact variance is inaccessible, and \cite{BasseAiroldi2018} supplies general interference nonconcentration logic; neither subsumes the equal-observation dense-PAME lower bound proved here. That lower bound holds on an additive no-interference subclass whose supports separately satisfy predictable-variation stability, and therefore transfers to the enlarged arbitrary-composition class. \cite{AronowGreenLee2014} gives sharp variance bounds for ordinary complete randomization, whereas global composition-table completion is a distinct unselected seed. \cite{BasseDingFellerToulis2024} and \cite{PuelzBasseFellerToulis2022} obtain exact tests by making peer-effect nulls sharp through symmetry or conditioning; PAME remains non-sharp from one random partition.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: Finite-sample CR2 conservativeness is not asserted: the exact bias is \(-C_{\tau\tau,n}\), and higher Johnson eigenvalues alternate in sign. Conservativeness emerges at the \(G_n\)-scale because only the negative degree-one eigenvalue survives. Predictable quadratic-variation stabilization is not a condition defining \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{dense}}\) and is not proved from bounded schedules; it is an additional filtration-side antecedent for general CLT and coverage statements. Its verification for the Rademacher lower-bound supports is construction-specific. The Rademacher variance limits separate only when \(\rho>0\); at \(\rho=0\) their gap vanishes. The \(O_{\mathbb P}(G_n^{-1/2})\) CR2 fluctuation bound is only an upper bound, so \(N_n\asymp n^{2/3}\) is a benchmark crossover rather than a proved exact noise-order elbow. Positive results remain restricted to the homogeneous fixed-size design.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The exact Kneser covariance, finite-sample design variance, schedule-uniform dense projection expansion, and CR2 variance and ratio expansions are unconditional design-based conclusions under their stated fixed-size design and boundedness conditions. The ambient class \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{dense}}\) additionally imposes scaled-variance nondegeneracy but does not impose predictable quadratic-variation stabilization. For every array in that class, the centered martingale CLT, CR2 studentized limits, Wald coverage, and sparse studentization conclusion are implications whose explicit additional antecedent is \(Q_n/\sigma_n^2\xrightarrow{p}1\); no claim is made that bounded schedules establish it. The sparse result drops \(N_n^2/n\to0\) but trades the comparator's Assumption 1 for that filtration-side premise. The exact software identity is tied to the stated equal-group unweighted intercept-plus-binary-treatment call and versioned package semantics. The impossibility theorem assumes \(G_n\to\infty\), \(p_n\to p\in(0,1)\), and \(N_n/n\to\rho\in(0,1]\). It holds on additive no-interference schedules and therefore transfers upward to arbitrary bounded composition interference; its support arrays satisfy predictable-variation stability by the separate Rademacher calculation even though the ambient class does not require it. When \(\rho=0\), the projection correction and Rademacher limit gap vanish. No finite-sample CR2 conservativeness or variable-group-size extension is asserted.

proofs.proof_tex:
We first prove both variance-estimator expansions without predictable quadratic-variation stability.  Define \(\pi_{1n}=p_n\) and \(\pi_{0n}=1-p_n\), fix \(z\in\{0,1\}\), and put \(m_n=G_{zn}=\pi_{zn}G_n\).  Group-count growth and stable treatment fractions imply \(m_n\to\infty\) and \(m_n\asymp G_n\).  Because \(N_n=MG_n\le n\), eventually \(n\ge2M\).

For a deterministic function \(f:\Omega_{n,M}\to\mathbb R\), define
\[
 \mu_n(f)=\mathbb E_nf,
 \qquad
 W_n(f)=\mathbb E_n[(f-mu_n(f))^2],
 \qquad
 C_n(f)=\operatorname{Cov}(f(A),f(C)),
\]
where \((A,C)\) is uniform over ordered disjoint pairs.  By Definition~\ref{def:random-partition-design} and independence of the complete treatment assignment, the arm-\(z\) groups, in their inherited order, are uniform over ordered pairwise-disjoint \(m_n\)-tuples.  Hence each one-group marginal is uniform on \(\Omega_{n,M}\), each distinct two-group marginal is a uniform ordered disjoint pair, and covariance expansion gives
\[
 \operatorname{Var}\!\left(\frac1{m_n}\sum_{j=1}^{m_n}f(A_j)\right)
 =\frac{W_n(f)}{m_n}+\frac{m_n-1}{m_n}C_n(f).
\tag{1}
\]

Theorem~\ref{thm:exact-kneser-identity} and orthogonality of the Johnson projections give
\[
 C_n(f)=\sum_{k=1}^M\lambda_{n,k}\|\Pi_{n,k}f\|_n^2,
 \qquad
 \sum_{k=1}^M\|\Pi_{n,k}f\|_n^2=W_n(f).
\tag{2}
\]
For \(1\le k\le M\), \(0\le j<k\), and \(n\ge2M\), all denominators are positive and
\[
 0\le\frac{M-j}{n-M-j}\le\frac{M}{n-M}\le1.
\]
The exact eigenvalue formula consequently implies
\[
 |\lambda_{n,k}|
 =\prod_{j=0}^{k-1}\frac{M-j}{n-M-j}
 \le\frac{M}{n-M}.
\]
Together with (2), this proves
\[
 |C_n(f)|\le\frac{M}{n-M}W_n(f).
\tag{3}
\]
Since \(n\ge MG_n\), one has \(M/(n-M)\le1/(G_n-1)\).  Equations (1)--(3) therefore yield
\[
 \operatorname{Var}\!\left(\frac1{m_n}\sum_{j=1}^{m_n}f(A_j)\right)
 \le W_n(f)\left(\frac1{m_n}+\frac1{G_n-1}\right).
\tag{4}
\]

Bounded potential outcomes give \(|h_{z,n}(A)|\le B\).  Thus the right side of (4) is \(O(G_n^{-1})\), uniformly in \(z\), first for \(f=h_{z,n}\) and then for \(f=h_{z,n}^2\).  Chebyshev's inequality, obtained from
\[
 \mathbf 1\{|X-\mathbb EX|>\varepsilon\}
 \le\frac{(X-\mathbb EX)^2}{\varepsilon^2},
\]
therefore gives
\[
 \frac1{m_n}\sum_{j=1}^{m_n}h_{z,n}(A_j)
   =\mathbb E_nh_{z,n}+o_p(1),
 \qquad
 \frac1{m_n}\sum_{j=1}^{m_n}h_{z,n}(A_j)^2
   =\mathbb E_nh_{z,n}^2+o_p(1).
\tag{5}
\]
Since \(m_n\to\infty\), the exact sample-variance identity and (5) imply
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 s_{z,n}^2
 &=\frac{m_n}{m_n-1}\left\{
 \frac1{m_n}\sum_{j=1}^{m_n}h_{z,n}(A_j)^2
 -\left(\frac1{m_n}\sum_{j=1}^{m_n}h_{z,n}(A_j)\right)^2
 \right\} \\
 &=\mathbb E_nh_{z,n}^2-(\mathbb E_nh_{z,n})^2+o_p(1)
 =V_{z,n}+o_p(1).
 \end{aligned}
\tag{6}
\]
Using \(G_{1n}=p_nG_n\), \(G_{0n}=(1-p_n)G_n\), and the fact that \(p_n\) is eventually bounded away from zero and one, (6) proves
\[
 G_n\widehat V_{\mathrm{CR2},n}
 =\frac{s_{1,n}^2}{p_n}+\frac{s_{0,n}^2}{1-p_n}
 =R_n+o_p(1).
\tag{7}
\]
No step through (7) uses predictable-variance stability.

Set
\[
 \Delta_n=R_n-\rho E_{\tau,1,n}.
\]
Theorem~\ref{thm:dense-projection-limit} gives
\[
 G_n\sigma_n^2=\Delta_n+o(1).
\tag{8}
\]
Subtracting (8) from (7) proves the second unconditional expansion,
\[
 G_n(\widehat V_{\mathrm{CR2},n}-\sigma_n^2)
 -\rho E_{\tau,1,n}=o_p(1).
\tag{9}
\]
Scaled-variance nondegeneracy and (8) imply \(\Delta_n\ge c_\sigma/2\) eventually.  Since \(E_{\tau,1,n}\ge0\), one has \(R_n\ge\Delta_n\).  Bounded outcomes and stable allocation also give \(R_n\le C\) for some finite constant \(C\): indeed \(V_{z,n}\le B^2\), while \(p_n\) and \(1-p_n\) are eventually bounded below by positive constants.  Writing
\[
 u_n=G_n\widehat V_{\mathrm{CR2},n}-R_n=o_p(1),
 \qquad
 v_n=G_n\sigma_n^2-\Delta_n=o(1),
\]
we obtain
\[
 \frac{\widehat V_{\mathrm{CR2},n}}{\sigma_n^2}-1
 =\frac{\rho E_{\tau,1,n}+u_n-v_n}{\Delta_n+v_n}
 =\frac{\rho E_{\tau,1,n}}{\Delta_n}+o_p(1).
\tag{10}
\]
The deterministic leading term in (10) is nonnegative.  Hence, for every \(\varepsilon>0\),
\[
 \Pr\!\left\{\frac{\widehat V_{\mathrm{CR2},n}}{\sigma_n^2}<1-\varepsilon\right\}\to0,
\]
which is the asserted asymptotic conservativeness.  Equation (10) also proves both directions of the ratio-consistency characterization.  If \(\rho E_{\tau,1,n}/\Delta_n\to0\), then the variance ratio converges to one in probability.  Conversely, if that deterministic nonnegative sequence does not converge to zero, it is bounded below by a positive constant on a subsequence, and (10) precludes convergence of the variance ratio to one on that subsequence.

Now impose the theorem's additional filtration-side premise \(Q_n/\sigma_n^2\xrightarrow{p}1\).  This premise has not been used in (1)--(10) and is not part of \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{dense}}\).  Put \(r_n=\Delta_n/R_n\).  The preceding bounds show that eventually
\[
 0<\frac{c_\sigma}{2C}\le r_n\le1.
\tag{11}
\]
Along any subsequence on which \(r_n\to r\in(0,1]\), (7)--(8) give
\[
 \frac{\sigma_n^2}{\widehat V_{\mathrm{CR2},n}}
 =\frac{\Delta_n+v_n}{R_n+u_n}\xrightarrow{p}r,
\tag{12}
\]
and in particular \(\Pr\{\widehat V_{\mathrm{CR2},n}>0\}\to1\).  Theorem~\ref{thm:centered-design-clt}, whose explicit extra antecedent is now satisfied, gives
\[
 X_n:=\frac{\widehat\tau_n-\tau_n}{\sigma_n}
 \rightsquigarrow\mathcal N(0,1).
\tag{13}
\]
Let \(b_n=(\sigma_n^2/\widehat V_{\mathrm{CR2},n})^{1/2}\) on the event of a positive denominator.  Equation (12) gives \(b_n\xrightarrow{p}\sqrt r\).  Convergence in distribution in (13) implies tightness, so \((b_n-\sqrt r)X_n\xrightarrow{p}0\): for any \(\eta>0\), choose \(K\) so that \(\limsup_n\Pr\{|X_n|>K\}<\eta\), and on \(\{|X_n|\le K\}\) bound the product by \(K|b_n-\sqrt r|\).  Applying the distribution-function sandwich at continuity points of the normal law therefore yields
\[
 \frac{\widehat\tau_n-\tau_n}
 {\sqrt{\widehat V_{\mathrm{CR2},n}}}
 =b_nX_n
 \rightsquigarrow\mathcal N(0,r).
\tag{14}
\]

Let \(z=z_{1-\alpha/2}\).  The zero-denominator event has probability tending to zero, and \(\{-z,z\}\) has zero probability under \(\mathcal N(0,r)\).  Thus (14) gives, along the chosen subsequence,
\[
 \Pr\{\tau_n\in I_{n,\alpha}^{\mathrm{CR2}}\}
 \longrightarrow
 2\Phi\!\left(\frac{z}{\sqrt r}\right)-1
 \ge2\Phi(z)-1=1-\alpha,
\tag{15}
\]
where the inequality follows from \(0<r\le1\).  Finally, (11) puts \((r_n)\) in a fixed compact subinterval of \((0,1]\).  Every subsequence therefore has a further subsequence on which (15) applies.  A failure of \(\liminf_n\Pr\{\tau_n\in I_{n,\alpha}^{\mathrm{CR2}}\}\ge1-\alpha\) would produce a subsequence, and hence a further convergent subsequence, contradicting (15).  This proves the conditional coverage conclusion.

Assume \(\rho=0\).  Theorem~\ref{thm:dense-projection-limit} then gives the unconditional variance expansion
\[
 G_n\sigma_n^2=R_n+o(1),
\tag{1}
\]
whereas the unconditional part of Theorem~\ref{thm:cr2-phase-frontier} gives
\[
 G_n\widehat V_{\mathrm{CR2},n}=R_n+o_p(1).
\tag{2}
\]
Scaled-variance nondegeneracy and (1) imply \(R_n\ge c_\sigma/2\) for all sufficiently large \(n\).  Dividing (2) by (1), with both denominators bounded away from zero after multiplication by \(G_n\), yields
\[
 \frac{\widehat V_{\mathrm{CR2},n}}{\sigma_n^2}\xrightarrow{p}1.
\tag{3}
\]

Now impose the additional filtration-side premise \(Q_n/\sigma_n^2\xrightarrow{p}1\).  It is not part of \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{dense}}\), and (1)--(3) did not use it.  Theorem~\ref{thm:centered-design-clt} applies under this premise and gives
\[
 \frac{\widehat\tau_n-\tau_n}{\sigma_n}
 \rightsquigarrow\mathcal N(0,1).
\tag{4}
\]
Equation (3) implies \((\sigma_n^2/\widehat V_{\mathrm{CR2},n})^{1/2}\xrightarrow{p}1\) and that the denominator is positive with probability tending to one.  Multiplying (4) by this factor and using the tightness argument from Theorem~\ref{thm:cr2-phase-frontier} proves
\[
 \frac{\widehat\tau_n-\tau_n}
 {\sqrt{\widehat V_{\mathrm{CR2},n}}}
 \rightsquigarrow\mathcal N(0,1).
\]

The only sampling-fraction condition used above is \(N_n/n\to0\), which is Assumption~\ref{ass:sampling-fraction} specialized to \(\rho=0\); no step invokes \(N_n^2/n\to0\).  The distinction is nonempty.  For example, set
\[
 N_n=M\left\lfloor\frac{n^{3/4}}{M}\right\rfloor,
 \qquad
 G_n=N_n/M.
\]
Then \(N_n\) is an integer multiple of the fixed group size \(M\), \(N_n\le n\) for all sufficiently large \(n\), and
\[
 \frac{N_n}{n}=n^{-1/4}(1+o(1))\to0,
 \qquad
 \frac{N_n^2}{n}=n^{1/2}(1+o(1))\to\infty.
\]
Subject to the other conditions defining \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{dense}}\), and to the theorem's separate predictable-variation premise, this sequence is covered.  Thus the result is an assumption trade for scalar inference; it neither derives predictable-variance stability from bounded schedules nor claims an assumption-free weakening of the comparator's whole-tuple condition.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
For every triangular array in \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{dense}}\), if the additional filtration-side premise \(Q_n/\sigma_n^2\xrightarrow{p}1\) holds under the design law, then
\[
\frac{\widehat\tau_n-\tau_n}{\sigma_n}\rightsquigarrow\mathcal N(0,1).
\]
Predictable-variance stability is not part of \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{dense}}\) and is not asserted to follow from bounded potential outcomes.  The only randomness is \((\mathbf A_n,\mathbf Z_n)\); the composition-indexed potential outcomes are fixed, and the Lindeberg condition is derived in \(\mathrm{Lemma}~\ref{lem:reveal-increment-bound}\) rather than assumed.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: After predictable quadratic-variation stability is removed from the ambient schedule class, the Gaussian conclusion must state that filtration-side condition as an explicit additional antecedent; bounded schedules alone do not derive it.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
For every array in \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{dense}}\), \(G_n\widehat V_{\mathrm{CR2},n}-R_n\xrightarrow{p}0\) and
\[
G_n(\widehat V_{\mathrm{CR2},n}-\sigma_n^2)-\rho E_{\tau,1,n}\xrightarrow{p}0.
\]
These two expansions do not require predictable quadratic-variation stability.  They imply that CR2 is asymptotically conservative and is ratio-consistent if and only if \(\rho E_{\tau,1,n}/(R_n-\rho E_{\tau,1,n})\to0\).  If additionally the filtration-side premise \(Q_n/\sigma_n^2\xrightarrow{p}1\) holds, then \(\liminf_n\Pr\{\tau_n\in I_{n,\alpha}^{\mathrm{CR2}}\}\ge1-\alpha\); moreover, along any subsequence on which \(r_n=(R_n-\rho E_{\tau,1,n})/R_n\to r\in(0,1]\), the CR2-studentized statistic converges to \(\mathcal N(0,r)\).  The additional premise is not part of \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{dense}}\) and is not asserted to follow from bounded potential outcomes.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The exact variance and CR2 expansions hold on the enlarged dense class, but studentization and Wald coverage require the separate predictable-variation antecedent used by the martingale CLT.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
For every array in \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{dense}}\) with \(\rho=0\), if additionally the filtration-side premise \(Q_n/\sigma_n^2\xrightarrow{p}1\) holds, then
\[
\frac{\widehat\tau_n-\tau_n}{\sqrt{\widehat V_{\mathrm{CR2},n}}}\rightsquigarrow\mathcal N(0,1)
\]
under \(N_n/n\to0\), with no condition on \(N_n^2/n\).  This is an assumption trade: it replaces the whole-tuple birthday condition in FuSamiiWang2026, Theorems 1--2, by the statistic-specific predictable-variation premise, which is neither part of \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{dense}}\) nor asserted to follow from bounded potential outcomes.  It includes grouped-unit counts such as \(N_n\asymp n^{3/4}\), for which \(N_n^2/n\to\infty\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The sparse scalar CLT remains valid without a birthday-scale condition only conditionally on predictable-variation stability, which is now external to the ambient dense class.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Predictable quadratic-variation stability is a filtration-side conditional premise for the martingale CLT, not a primitive property derived for every bounded dense schedule.  The replacement removes only that condition and retains all other class restrictions.
